title: Staged kernel manifest + on-demand symbol relay for mixed CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a safer, staged approach to roll out updated CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS artifacts to heterogeneous inference fleets. This ticket implements a signed staged kernel manifest with per-host on-demand symbol relay (a lightweight runtime layer that maps unresolved symbols to staged artifacts) and a delta-patch rollback path. Goals: 1) reduce blast radius for kernel/library upgrades; 2) support partial rollout by capability (arch, driver version, memory profile); 3) provide a verifiable prelink step and fast safe rollback; 4) minimize cold-start latency impact by doing lazy mapping only for missing symbols. Non-goals: replacing the existing kernel cache, changing compilation toolchain, or modifying model-level GEMM dispatch heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Manifest can express staged artifacts by tag+hash with per-arch selectors (sm_80/sm_86/sm_90) and rollout percentage. 2) Runtime can fetch and atomically install a staged artifact with signature verification. 3) On-demand symbol relay resolves missing symbols without full re-link; end-to-end request latency impact < 5% p50 and < 15% p99 in controlled canary. 4) Automated delta rollback restores previous manifest and artifacts within 60s without container restart. 5) Integration tests exercise signed manifests, invalid signature rejection, and rollback.
work_items: add manifest signer and verification CLI
update agent bootstrap to honor staged manifests
risks: improper signature verification allowing unsigned artifacts
increased cold-start when many missing symbols trigger relay
edge cases on very old drivers causing unresolved relocations
mitigations: require KMS-signed manifest for any staged rollout; reject unsigned in prod by default
adaptive probe: if more than N relays happen in T seconds degrade to full prelink path
driver compatibility whitelist and preflight tests in canary
qa_plan: Unit tests for signer/verifier; e2e in canary cluster (10 nodes) exercising mixed driver versions; fuzz invalid manifests; chaos test network partition during manifest install
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Canary on internal fleet (5% of runtime nodes) with telemetry. 3) Expand by region/arch buckets using manifest selectors. 4) Run 24h perf/regression gates. 5) Start 10% weekly expansion; emergency rollback via manifest pinning.
monitoring: telemetry events for manifest.apply, manifest.verify.fail, relay.resolve.count, relay.resolve.latency; alert if relay.resolve.count spikes or manifest.apply failures > 0.5% in 1h
notes: Initial design reviewed with runtime and infra on 2026-02-28; Security flagged KMS integration and requested threat model. Design doc updated to include minimal attack surface for relay process. Diego to prototype signer CLI and a shim library by 2026-03-08.
